title: Perinatal taurine depletion increases oxidative stress in adult female rats

sections.abstract: <jats:p>Our previous studies and those of others demonstrate that perinatal taurine exposure affects adult physiology and susceptibility to disease in several animal models of cardiovascular and renal disease. Perinatal taurine depletion typically produces adult disorders, but perinatal taurine supplementation minimally influences normal physiology in adults. This study tests the hypothesis that perinatal taurine depletion leads to increased oxidative stress in adult female rats. Female Sprague‐Dawley rats were fed normal rat chow with 3% β‐alanine (taurine deficient, TD), 3% taurine (taurine supplemented, TS) or water alone (C) from conception to weaning. Their female offspring were fed normal rat chow and water alone throughout the experiment. At 7–8 weeks of age, body, kidney and heart weights were not significantly different among groups (n = 10/group). Neither did their plasma sodium, plasma potassium, mean arterial pressure and heart rate. Compared to control, plasma malondialdehyde levels (a bio‐marker of oxidative stress from lipid peroxidation) were significantly higher in TD and the TS group was intermediate between the other two groups, i.e., not significantly different than either. These results suggest that perinatal taurine depletion increases oxidative stress in adult female rats and could play a role in the morbidity of these animals as they mature through adulthood.</jats:p>
